notes: Real English speech with published reference transcripts, unlike P5 (synthetic tones/chirp/harmonics, no ground truth). Source: LibriSpeech dev-clean (OpenSLR SLR12), 10 chapters / 4 speakers, streamed from https://www.openslr.org/resources/12/dev-clean.tar.gz and aborted after 30 MB (338 MB total). Audio decoded to 16 kHz mono fp32 by ffmpeg (no soundfile/librosa/torchaudio on this box; the HF `librispeech_asr_dummy` mirror now only ships a parquet shard, unreadable without pyarrow).

Split: 40 calibration utterances build the permutation pi per layer and calibrate theta_l (quantile of permuted block energies, target tau of (token, block) pairs); 60 disjoint utterances are evaluated. All WER/CER/exact-match numbers are on the evaluation split only.

WER/CER use a local two-row Levenshtein (no jiwer) on local lowercase/punctuation strip-normalized text; values are per-utterance rates averaged over utterances (mean +- sample std, ddof=1), with wer_corpus (total edits / total reference words) reported alongside.

exact_match = fraction of utterances whose hypothesis tokenization equals the reference tokenization exactly (whisper tokenizer on the normalized hypothesis vs the normalized reference). It is a strict metric: dense whisper-base itself is not 1.0 (0.000).

teacher_forced_top1 = argmax agreement between the gated and dense decoder logits when both are teacher-forced on the prompt + the *reference* tokens, so unlike P5's free-running agreement it is a label-bearing metric. enc_rel_l2 is the relative L2 between the gated and dense encoder output, averaged over utterances.

Timing is CPU only (torch.set_num_threads(32), 16-core Zen 5 / 32 SMT threads): the full 6-layer audio encoder (no lm_head) and the full decoder loop (prefill + greedy steps up to <|eot|>). Values are ms/utterance, median over repeated rounds that alternate configs round-robin so drift hits all configs alike. tau=-1 is the unmodified dense model (original fc2.forward); tau=0 keeps every block but still permutes, and is verified isomorphic to dense before any result is reported.

The honest wall-clock result: the per-token gate still executes a dense fc1 and a dense fc2 GEMM inside PyTorch (mask + gather + alpha), so PyTorch-level E2E shows no speedup. The AVX-512 kernel mounts the *real* 32-lane skipping down-projection (down_skip_avx512_auto2), verified to match the PyTorch gated path, which removes the skipped tiles from fc2; fc1 remains dense, so the encoder gain is bounded by fc2's share of the pass.

dead-block numbers are the fraction of 32-lane blocks with *exactly* zero energy in the fc2 input, measured on every selected utterance (calib + eval), before (natural lane order) and after (pi order) the permutation; mean +- std across utterances. This replaces P5's single-clip 51-54% claim on enc.4/enc.5 with the real distribution over utterances.

`energy_captured` / `actual_skip` are measured on exactly the quantity the gate thresholds (block L2 in pi order). At tau=0.6 WER is 0.070 vs 0.061 dense: the mechanism is not free, and the trade is now measured in absolute WER/CER instead of dense-vs-gated agreement.
